Referral Note

24-year-old graduate student with four ED visits over eight months for intermittent right lower extremity weakness and episodes of slow, slurred speech. Complete neurological workup normal. Referring for psychiatric evaluation; patient is frustrated and fears a missed neurological diagnosis.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Appropriately groomed and dressed. Appears stated age.

Behavior: Cooperative, maintains appropriate eye contact. No abnormal movements observed at rest.

Speech: Normal rate and volume; becomes mildly slowed when discussing academic stress, then normalizes.

Mood / Affect: States mood is 'frustrated'; affect congruent.

Thought / Perception: Linear, logical, goal-directed. No delusions, obsessions, or perceptual disturbances. Denies SI/HI.

Cognition / Insight: Alert, oriented ×4. Insight limited regarding stress–symptom relationship; judgment intact.

2. Discuss the single most important differential diagnosis.
Explain why this diagnosis was considered and why it was ruled out using evidence from the patient presentation.
3. Present your initial evidence-based treatment recommendations.
